dedupe_keys.name: era5 based global meteorological wildfire danger maps

description: ERA5-based global meteorological wildfire danger maps is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Claudia Vitolo et al. Forest fires are an integral part of the natural Earth system dynamics, however they are becoming more devastating and less predictable as anthropogenic climate change exacerbates their impacts. In order to advance fire science, fire danger reanalysis products can be used as proxy for fire weather observations with the advantage of being homogeneously distributed both in space and time. Coverage: global; published in 2020. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 3604 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support emergency-service and public-facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
